name: TMC2209-LA-T
title: Two-phase bipolar stepper motor driver, STEP/DIR with single-wire UART, 2.8 A peak
summary: The TMC2209 drives one two-phase bipolar stepper motor from 4.75 V to 29 V with two integrated H-bridges of 170 mΩ per switch, up to 2 A RMS (2.8 A peak) per coil. Motion comes from STEP and DIR inputs, interpolated to 256 microsteps, or from an internal step generator. It offers a silent voltage-mode chopper (StealthChop2) and a cycle-by-cycle current chopper (SpreadCycle), sensorless load and stall measurement (StallGuard4), load-adaptive current (CoolStep), current sensing by external resistors or by MOSFET on-resistance, and configuration by pins, OTP or a single-wire UART. It comes in a 5 mm x 5 mm QFN28 with exposed pad.
key_figures: 4.75 V to 29 V (5.5 V to 29 V with the internal regulator)
1.4 A RMS design guideline, 2.0 A RMS with duty limit, 2.8 A peak

circuits.title: Standard application circuit
circuits.description: The driver with external sense resistors. The 5 V regulator output carries 2.2 µF, the charge pump has 22 nF between CPO and CPI and 100 nF from VCP to VS, and the motor supply is filtered with two 100 nF ceramics and a 100 µF low-ESR electrolytic. RSA and RSB from BRA and BRB to ground set the coil current. VREF scales the current or stays open. Logic inputs are strapped to GND or VCC_IO, or driven by the controller; VCC_IO has its own 100 nF.

circuits.description: The standard circuit without sense resistors: BRA and BRB go straight to the ground plane and the MOSFET on-resistance measures the coil current. A resistor RREF from 5VOUT to VREF sets a reference current that fixes the motor current. Internal sensing (GCONF.1 or OTP0.6) must be set while ENN is high, before the driver is enabled.

circuits.title: 5V only operation
circuits.description: Running from a single 4.7 V to 5.4 V supply. The regulator output gets 10 µF, and an optional 10 Ω from the supply to 5VOUT bridges the internal regulator and forms an RC filter against chopper ripple. With that resistor fitted the supply becomes the reference for the motor current and must stay at or below 5.5 V, and standby no longer works. VREF is left open; sense resistors set the current.

circuits.title: Simple ESD enhancement
circuits.description: Small capacitors from each motor output to ground slow the edge of an ESD hit on the motor lines; values from 100 pF to 1 nF work, larger ones absorb more but add switching loss, most at high supply voltage. Each sense resistor gets 100 nF in parallel.

circuits.title: Motor output protection with LC filters and varistors
circuits.description: Each motor output passes through a 50 Ω (at 100 MHz) inductor and then carries 470 pF to ground on the motor side, decoupling the driver from the connector. A varistor across each coil (V1, V2) clamps the coil voltage when a motor is plugged or unplugged live; four more varistors from each line to ground are an option for heavy ESD. Varistors are chosen for the supply voltage.

circuits.title: Two drivers on one UART with different addresses
circuits.description: A microcontroller UART runs a single-wire bus: TXD reaches the bus through 1 kΩ and RXD sits on the bus, so the master hears its own transmission and the drivers' replies. Both drivers' PDN_UART pins are on the bus. The first leaves MS1_AD0 and MS2_AD1 open (pull-downs, address 0); the second ties MS1_AD0 to VCC_IO (address 1). Both can be read and written.

circuits.title: Drivers sharing one address, write only
circuits.description: Drivers with the same address all listen to the master's TXD on their PDN_UART pins and take the same settings in parallel, as one device; nothing is read back.

circuits.title: Addressing many drivers through analog switches
circuits.description: Each driver's PDN_UART has a 22 kΩ pull-up to VIO and joins the shared bus through one switch of a 74HC4066, closed by its own port pin, like slave selects on SPI. TXD reaches the bus through 1 kΩ and RXD sits on it; an optional 74HC1G125 buffer, enabled by a further port pin, drives the bus from TXD for long lines or many drivers. The bus carries on to more drivers.
notes: The buffer's enable is active low: the port pin goes low to transmit.

circuits.title: Fixed resistor divider to set current scale
circuits.description: A divider R1/R2 from 5VOUT or a precision reference sets 1 V to 2.4 V on VREF for a fixed current scale; R1+R2 is about 10 kΩ, and an external reference improves precision. An optional BC847, switched through 100 kΩ by a digital line, pulls R3 to ground to lower the scale.

circuits.title: Precision current scaler
circuits.description: An 8-bit DAC referenced to a 2.5 V precision reference drives VREF with 0 V to 2.4 V under digital control.

circuits.title: Simple PWM based current scaler
circuits.description: A microcontroller PWM above 20 kHz is smoothed by 22 kΩ and 1 µF into 0 V to 2.4 V on VREF; the duty cycle sets the current scale.

circuits.title: Layout example schematic
circuits.description: A complete board around the driver. The motor supply has an SMB28A TVS, two 330 µF 50 V electrolytics, 100 nF and two 10 µF ceramics, and 1 µF in series with 1100 mΩ (R301). The charge pump uses 22 nF and 100 nF. Sense resistors of 120 mΩ 1 W sit on BRA and BRB, each with an open solder jumper across it for internal sensing, and test points. 5VOUT carries 2.2 µF and an SMBJ5A, with an open jumper JP303 to +VM for 5 V only use. UART_TX reaches PDN_UART through 1 kΩ and UART_RX reads the pin directly. Three-pin headers select internal or external STEP and DIR. STDBY is pulled down by 100 kΩ, SPREAD has an unfitted pull-up to VCC_IO, and DIAG lights a white LED through 220 Ω.
notes: Shorting jumpers U302 and U303 (2.54 mm) plug onto J301 and J302 to pick internal or external STEP and DIR.

where.20 mΩ: internal resistance from BRxy to the comparator
where.VVREF: voltage on VREF, 2.5 V or open gives full scale

where.CS: current scale from IRUN or IHOLD, 0…31
where.VFS: full-scale sense voltage set by vsense (VSRTL, VSRTH), 325 mV by default

equations.name: Lower coil current limit for StealthChop2 automatic tuning
equations.expr: ILower Limit = tBLANK × fPWM × VM / RCOIL
equations.note: RCOIL = 5 Ω, VM = 24 V, TBL=%01 (24 clocks), PWM_FREQ=%00 (2/1024 clocks): 24/512 × 24 V / 5 Ω = 225 mA, the least run current for tuning.

equations.name: Effective PWM voltage

where.248: sine wave peak in the table

equations.note: UPWM is the RMS value, peak/√2.

where.MSPR: microsteps per rotation, e.g. 51200 for 256 µsteps and 200 fullsteps

where.HoldingTorque: torque with both coils at ICOILNOM

equations.note: In SI units CBEMF equals the torque constant numerically; the factor 2 is there because the rating assumes a fullstep position with both coils on, and the result is RMS volts per coil.

equations.name: Slow decay time setting
equations.note: 25 kHz chopper with half the cycle in two slow decay phases: tOFF = 1/25 kHz × 50/100 × 1/2 = 10 µs, giving TOFF=3 at 12 MHz and 4.25 (4 or 5) at 16 MHz.

equations.name: StealthChop PWM frequency
equations.note: Chosen by PWM_FREQ = %00 … %11; each motor output switches at half fPWM.

equations.note: 0.715 Hz per LSB with the internal 12 MHz clock.

equations.name: UART CRC polynomial
equations.note: CRC8-ATM, start value 0, applied LSB first over every byte including sync and address; per bit the register shifts left and takes in CRC.7 ^ CRC.1 ^ CRC.0 ^ incoming bit; in byte code, XOR with 0x07 when the shifted-out bit differs from the data bit.

equations.note: IRUN=31, IHOLD=16, IHOLDDELAY=4: about 1 s at 16 MHz.

operation.text: Three ways to use it: as a plain STEP/DIR driver set up by pins, with VREF for current and INDEX and DIAG as feedback; as a STEP/DIR driver whose defaults have been programmed into OTP or loaded over UART after each power-up (a TXD line alone, or bit-banging, can set many drivers at once); or with PDN_UART on a bidirectional UART, which replaces ENN, DIAG, INDEX, MS1, MS2 and VREF so that STEP, DIR and PDN_UART are enough.

Single-wire, half-duplex, with CRC. It turns on by itself when valid datagrams arrive. The baud rate is found from each datagram's sync nibble: 9000 baud minimum (worst case 20 MHz clock), up to fCLK/16. Four addresses come from MS1_AD0 and MS2_AD1. Frames match the TMC5130, TMC516x and TMC5072. Write-only registers need a shadow copy in the master for read-modify-write. With UART in use, set GCONF.pdn_disable because the line must idle high.

Write: 64 bits — sync nibble 1010 plus four reserved bits, slave address 0…3, register address with bit 7 set, 32 data bits high byte first, CRC. Read request: 32 bits — sync, address, register address with bit 7 clear, CRC. The reply is 64 bits with address 0xFF, sent after SENDDELAY (8 bit times by default) at the master's baud rate; the output switches off four bit times after its last stop bit. Bytes are LSB first with start and stop bits. A gap of more than 63 bit times between start bits resets the receiver, which then needs 12 idle bit times; pulses shorter than 16 clocks count as glitches, and a CRC error is treated the same. The baud rate cannot be cut to below 15 % of the previous value in one step. Each accepted write increments IFCNT.

Up to four drivers can share a bus by address. More need analog switches as selects, which leaves MS1 and MS2 free for resolution as long as the address they make is accounted for. Drivers given the same settings can all be written at once without addressing. With the optional buffer, SENDDELAY must leave the master time to release the bus; the master also receives everything it sends.

Each active STEP edge moves the microstep counter by the selected resolution, up when DIR was low and down when high; DEDGE makes both edges active to halve the step rate. Inputs are synchronised to the clock and filtered against glitches; long or cabled lines need filtering or differential transmission. Resolution can change at any time: the sequencer jumps to the nearest position of the new resolution, so steps stay symmetrical in both directions.

MicroPlyer splits each input step into equal 1/256 microsteps timed from the previous step interval. The longest interval is 2^20 clocks, so at 12 MHz step rates below roughly 12 Hz count as standstill; stst then sets and, if PDN_UART allows, current reduction begins. It needs a jitter-free step rate.

1024 sine entries cover one electrical turn (four fullsteps). Fullstep uses positions 128, 384, 640, 896 (both coils at 70.7 %), half step starts at 64 in steps of 128, quarter step starts at 32 in steps of 64; zero-current and full-current positions are never used.

INDEX goes active when coil A's sine crosses zero going positive, once per electrical period (four fullsteps); with a home switch it pins homing to one microstep. It can instead show the overtemperature prewarning or toggle on each internal generator step.

Writing a non-zero VACTUAL runs the motor at that velocity with direction from the sign; STEP/DIR and the generator can be mixed. There is no ramp: above the motor's start/stop speed the master must change VACTUAL in small steps. Steps can be counted on INDEX (GCONF.index_step) or by polling MSCNT.

A voltage-mode PWM chopper, silent at standstill and low speed. Automatic tuning learns the motor in two stages: AT#1 at standstill with run current for over 130 ms sets PWM_OFS_AUTO; AT#2 at a steady medium speed with real back-EMF (typically 60-300 RPM) adjusts PWM_GRAD_AUTO by one per 8 fullsteps. Tuning carries on during later motion. Changing VREF or VS invalidates it until the next AT#1. A minimum TPOWERDOWN of 2 is needed. IRUN should be 8 to 31; use vsense for lower currents. The automatic mode is recommended; the feed-forward mode (pwm_autoscale=0) needs UART and well-known motor and supply.

With pwm_autoscale the driver measures coil current during the on time and a proportional loop with gain PWM_REG trims PWM_SCALE_AUTO. A small PWM_REG is stable; faster acceleration in AT#2 needs a larger one. Current can only be measured above a minimum duty cycle set by blank time and PWM frequency, so the minimum regulated current rises with supply voltage and PWM frequency. Lower currents after tuning follow from the learned offset and gradient; freewheeling reaches zero.

TPWMTHRS switches to SpreadCycle above a velocity (and back below it with 1/16 hysteresis); it can be set in OTP for standalone use. Switch at low speed, since back-EMF shifts current against voltage by up to 90° and causes a jerk, even overcurrent, at higher speed. StealthChop keeps its last regulation state while in SpreadCycle, so supply and threshold should not change much meanwhile. Enable StealthChop first at standstill for at least 128 chopper periods. A stall or abrupt stop in StealthChop can raise current for tens of milliseconds and trip short detection; clear flags and restart from zero speed.

Current-based flags react slowly in StealthChop. ola and olb show whether full current is reached on each coil: flicker comes from coil or sense asymmetry, steady means an open coil, both can show without a motor or above the PWM limit. PWM_SCALE_SUM at 255 means the supply cannot drive the full current.

With IHOLD=0 in StealthChop, FREEWHEEL picks normal hold, freewheeling, or a short across each coil through the low-side or high-side MOSFETs, active after TPOWERDOWN and IHOLDDELAY. Shorting gives eddy-current braking at no power but lets a constant torque turn the motor slowly. Regulation freezes at zero current so restart is quick.

A cycle-by-cycle current chopper: on phase until the comparator trips, slow decay timed by TOFF, fast decay, then a second slow decay. Blanking hides switching spikes for one or two microseconds. 16 kHz to 30 kHz suits most motors. Hysteresis is set as HSTRT+HEND at the start of each cycle, stepping down every 16 clocks to HEND, which keeps the frequency out of the audio band. Start with low hysteresis and raise HSTRT until the current is smooth through zero; an effective hysteresis around 4 fits most motors. Very high speeds may gain from TOFF 1 or 2 with TBL 0 or 1. Above roughly 2 A peak, body-diode conduction slightly distorts the SpreadCycle current wave at medium speed; StealthChop does not show this.

Choose RSENSE for the full current at VREF 2.5 V and IRUN 31. Use low-inductance film or composition parts, laid out symmetrically with short, equal traces, and never a shared ground path between the two. The resistor carries peak coil current at standstill; 0.5 W covers most uses to 1.2 A RMS, 0.25 W with vsense=1.

With I_scale_analog (default) VREF is amplified, filtered (3.5 kHz bandwidth inside) and used as reference: 2.5 V to 5 V gives full scale, below that the current scales linearly. Below about 0.5 V to 1 V noise hurts precision; best is full current with VREF near 2 V to 2.4 V. A divider, a DAC, or a PWM above 10 kHz through an RC filter with a time constant of several milliseconds can drive it.

Setting internal_Rsense (GCONF or OTP) uses the MOSFET on-resistance instead of sense resistors; BRA and BRB then go straight to ground at the package. A resistor RREF from 5VOUT to VREF sets the reference current, amplified 3000 times. Temperature drift is compensated, but with high currents a gradient inside the die gives around 10 % overshoot for about a second at heat-up. Best with StealthChop and up to 1.4 A RMS; SpreadCycle can show chopper noise at high die temperature. Trace resistance on BR pins adds to the result, so calibrate in the application.

Load measurement for StealthChop: SG_RESULT falls with load, near-linearly, to a motor-specific low at 90° load angle. It updates each fullstep. DIAG pulses when SG_RESULT drops to twice SGTHRS, only in StealthChop and while TCOOLTHRS ≥ TSTEP > TPWMTHRS. Tune by loading the motor at working speed, start SGTHRS at half the lowest value seen before stall, and check from 80 % to 120 % of speed and across temperature. It is unreliable at very low speed (often under one turn per second) and where back-EMF exceeds the supply.

Adjusts current to load using SG_RESULT: below SEMIN×32 the current rises by SEUP steps, at or above (SEMIN+SEMAX+1)×32 it falls by one step per SEDN readings, between IRUN and 1/2 or 1/4 of IRUN (SEIMIN). It runs above TCOOLTHRS velocity and only in StealthChop. Energy savings up to 75 %; half the current is a quarter of the power. Rising current can cause false stall detection, so disable CoolStep while homing with StallGuard.

PDN_UART low enables automatic reduction: after stst and TPOWERDOWN (20 × 2^18 clocks by default) the current steps down to IHOLD, IHOLDDELAY setting the step rate. The default goes to slightly over half the run current, cutting standstill dissipation below 33 %.

STDBY high switches off the 5 V regulator and all internal blocks, about 2 mW at 12 V and under 1 mW at 5 V. Stop the motor first, hold ENN and VREF low during standby, and keep VCC_IO on (it may drop to 1.5 V). Registers return to power-up defaults on leaving standby.
On-resistance losses rise with the square of current and MOSFET resistance rises about 50 % per 100 °C, so PCB thermal design becomes critical at or above 1.4 A RMS for long periods.

A four-level sensor gives prewarning and shutdown; thresholds are set by OTTRIM (UART or OTP). After ot trips the driver stays off until the temperature is below the prewarning level. Heat travels across the die with delay, so gross overcurrent can damage the IC before the sensor reacts.

Every power MOSFET's current is checked; a short must be seen three times before the bridge shuts off, to ignore ESD. The affected bridge goes off and s2ga/s2gb or s2vsa/s2vsb set; disable and re-enable the driver to restart.

Open load is flagged when the target coil current cannot be reached, so undervoltage, high speed, shorts or overtemperature can also set it. Read it at low or nominal speed, preferably in SpreadCycle; it is informative and the driver does not act on it.

DIAG goes high for stall detection (when enabled), and latches drv_err for overtemperature or short circuit; power-on reset, charge pump undervoltage and power stage disable (ENN) also drive it. Disabling the power stage resets the latch.
Write the byte, bit and magic code 0xbd to OTP_PROG for each bit, wait 10 ms or more, check OTP_READ, and reprogram missing bits with 100 ms. VS must be at least 6 V. Bits can only be set.

Power-on reset loads defaults and OTP values. To reset, cycle VS, 5VOUT (only through VS) or most simply VCC_IO; inputs must be held low meanwhile because their protection diodes clamp to VCC_IO, or have series resistors.

CLK tied to GND near the IC selects the internal oscillator, factory-trimmed to 12 MHz. An external clock of 8 to 13.4 MHz (max. 16 MHz, near 50 % duty, clean CMOS levels) takes over at its first rising edge; down to 4 MHz saves power and emissions at some cost in performance. If the external clock stops for 32 internal clocks the driver falls back to the internal one. A shared clock synchronises several drivers.

Solder the die pad to a solid ground plane with many vias; the ground below the pad acts as star point and the top layer should spread heat into a large ground plane. Sense resistors see steps down to 0.5 mV: place them close, give each its own via(s) to ground, carry no other current on their returns. Put the 2.2 µF to 4.7 µF 5VOUT ceramic right at the pin with its own direct return to the pad or nearest GND pin. Decouple VS with 47 µF or more electrolytic plus a ceramic close to the device; at least 100 µF near the driver is recommended, low ESR, and its ripple current also depends on the supply's impedance and cable. Keep the fast motor traces away from high-impedance signals.
VCC_IO can come from 5VOUT or from an external rail such as a 3.3 V regulator.
ESD from motors, plastic housings and belts can reach several kV and reset or destroy the driver; grounding the motor bodies or using conductive plastic avoids it.
